grammar.title: The Passive: All Tenses and Passive Infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The passive is **be** + past participle. To make any tense passive, put **be** in that tense.

For example, we say **is being painted**, **has been finished**, and **will be announced**.

With modals, use modal + **be** + past participle, like **must be signed** and **can be done**.

For the past, use modal + **have been** + past participle, like **should have been sent**.

The passive infinitive is **to be** + past participle, and the passive -ing form is **being** + past participle.

With verbs like give and offer, either object can become the subject, so **I was given** a prize is common.

Use the passive to focus on the action, not the person, and in formal writing. In informal English, **get** + past participle is common for bad things, like **got fired**.

Avoid perfect continuous passives like **has been being built**. They are very rare.
examples: *The kitchen **is being redecorated** this week.* (present continuous passive)
*Over 200 people **have been invited** to the wedding.* (present perfect passive)
*The match **will be shown** live on TV.* (will passive)
*Phones **must be switched off** during the exam.* (modal passive)
*She expects **to be promoted** next year.* (passive infinitive)

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: The restaurant confirmed Sara's booking.
practice.a: Sara's booking was confirmed by the restaurant.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: The ambitious student will finish the project tomorrow.
practice.a: The project will be finished by the ambitious student tomorrow.

practice.q: Rewrite using the passive infinitive: She expects the company to promote her next year.
practice.a: She expects to be promoted next year.
